title: the scratch sweep never reads a live process as a dead minter on Windows
intention: store.process_start answers the creation time of a RUNNING pid on Windows (GetProcessTimes), None for a pid that is gone, so minter_alive is True for a live process and sweep_scratch never drops the live scratch tables of the process that calls it.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 on akiendell: process_start reads /proc, which Windows lacks, so it answered None for every pid. minter_alive then read the caller's OWN process as dead, and sweep_scratch() from a process holding one live scratch table dropped it and unregistered it (probe: sweep dropped 1, table gone, not registered). The tester sweeps before every --seal (cli.py:701), so test_the_seal_announces_itself lost its fixture bus families mid-run; the bus re-created its tables unregistered; each transit table was then dropped by name at exit and each _delivery companion, with no registry row to find it by, outlived the run: 24 seal_ann_*_delivery tables on the cairn database, 3 more per run (21 -> 24 measured), the orphan ticket 9484180b4ff4. Linux is unaffected (it reads /proc); this is the Windows branch the 2026-09-06 scratch design (201a37bf1613) never had.
traces_to: Law 4 (a scratch table that cannot outlive its process must not die under it either), Law 3.
how: D1: _windows_process_start(pid) via ctypes kernel32: OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION), GetExitCodeProcess (STILL_ACTIVE 259, because a handle to an exited process still opens), GetProcessTimes creation FILETIME to epoch seconds, None when the pid cannot be opened; process_start dispatches to it when os.name == 'nt' and reads /proc elsewhere unchanged. D2: a proof, three teeth. Red-first on Windows.

clauses.claim: process_start of a running child is its creation time (within a minute of now) and minter_alive is True for this process and for the child
process_start of a pid that has exited is None and minter_alive is False for it
sweep_scratch() leaves this process's own live scratch table standing and registered

decisions.text: D1: the Windows branch of process_start.
D2: the proof, one tooth per clause.

measured.saw: process_start(own pid) = None and minter_alive(own pid, now) = False on Windows; sweep_scratch() dropped the caller's own live scratch table (dropped 1, table gone, not registered)
measured.how: scratch script over store.scratch, scratchpad ma.py, venv python on akiendell

measured.saw: bisect: during test_the_seal_announces_itself the cairn_scratch registry held 0 seal_ann rows while 3 transit + 3 _delivery tables stood; after _SCRATCH.close() the 3 _delivery tables remained
measured.how: scratchpad bis.py, REGISTRY query before close

measured.saw: after the fix one run of the leaking proof adds 0 tables (before: +3); the 36 existing orphans (empty, owner bus, no registry row) were dropped through store.drop_table on this box
measured.how: 9484180b4ff4's proof tooth 1, red unfixed, green fixed; clean.py

measured.saw: UNMEASURED on Linux: expected unaffected because process_start reads /proc there; the Dell reproduction akienasus offered would confirm 0 leaked tables per run
